title: Catalog entry
description: One operation, described so an agent can find it among thousands. Every required field is required because a measurement said so, and the reason is on the field. See docs/catalog-entry-spec.md for the numbers.

name.description: Stable identifier. It is the key a plan step, a binding and `run_operation` all use, so renaming one is a breaking change for all three.

status.description: `available` means it runs today; `planned` means the entry exists so an agent is told the capability is known and absent, rather than inferring it from silence.

tool.description: The dedicated MCP tool, or null when the operation is reached through `run_operation`. A dedicated tool is a promotion, not the default: the exposed tool list has a ceiling that the catalog does not.

category.description: FACET. The family. Measured the single most informative one: declaring it alone cuts 800 candidates to 23 and takes found@3 from 20% to 70%.

produces.description: FACET. What the caller gets back. Measured worth 15 points of found@3 on top of the input kind, and it is the facet a caller always knows: they know whether they want a file, a number, or a description.

applicability.description: FACET. What the operation can be pointed at, and how much of it. These are the declarations a caller can answer from their own situation without knowing the vocabulary of the catalogue they are searching.

inputs.description: `none` is not an empty list: it means the operation takes no dataset at all, and such an entry is kept for every input kind rather than dropped from all of them.

requires_projected_crs.description: True when the engine REFUSES a geographic CRS. Checked by executing the operation on a geographic dataset, not by reading the source: reading it once reported five operations that do not refuse, because the word appeared in their warnings.

dataset_inputs.description: How many datasets the operation consumes: 0 for one that takes none, 1 for a single layer, 2 for one that combines two. A caller knows this about their own situation without knowing anything about the catalogue, which is what makes it a facet rather than a label. It became REQUIRED on 2026-08-29, when a catalogue growing from 51 to 61 operations pushed the commonest surviving set from 26 candidates to 34 -- past the point where the whole set can be handed to the caller -- and the measured effect was that the right operation stopped being delivered 100% of the time and fell to 45%. Adding capability had made discovery worse. Arity took the median surviving set from 34 to 9 and found@3 from 36% to 60%. Derive it from the operation's own signature and check it against that, rather than declaring it by hand: a wrong value makes the operation invisible to every caller who describes their situation correctly, with no error anywhere. `null` means the arity is variable or not expressible as a count -- a list of inputs, or inputs named inside a query string -- and an entry declaring it MUST be kept for every declared arity rather than dropped from all of them, the same rule `inputs: ["none"]` follows. Declaring 1 for an n-ary operation is the failure this guards: the first version of this field said 1 for a merge that takes a list, and it vanished for every caller holding two layers.

geometry.description: The geometry families the operation's vector input(s) accept, as a set; absent means any geometry, and such an entry is kept for every family. A caller declaring the families it holds keeps only the entries accepting all of them. Declared only where the operation refuses the other families, because a declaration hides the entry from callers holding them: tests/test_geometry_declarations.py holds each one to the refusal.

workload.description: Which execution profile the dispatcher would route this to. Declared before routing needs it, so the day it does the catalog is already the input.

summary.description: One sentence: what it does and the one thing that would surprise you. Read by humans and indexed by both ranking engines.

description.description: The full account, written for an agent deciding whether to call it: what it needs, what it refuses, and what it records. Say what goes wrong silently if it is used incorrectly.

phrasings.description: How somebody NAMES THE PROBLEM, never a synonym of the operation's name. 'too many vertices', not 'simplify'. Honest note: measured at no effect on queries written afterwards, and kept because it costs nothing and because writing it forces the author to think about how somebody would look for this.

distinguishes.description: RECOMMENDED, and the field that matters most inside a crowded family. Contrastive text: what this is NOT, and which neighbour does that instead. The facets narrow 800 candidates to about 20 of the same family, and inside that residue ranking is close to random — this is what separates them. Write 'not X, which does Y', never a restatement of the summary.

description.description: Where a wrong value fails SILENTLY, say so here. A parameter with no safe default should have no default, and this is where the reason lives.

examples.description: At least two, and the first one is load-bearing: it is the probe the discoverability contract runs. Write the GOAL a caller has, not the invocation — the test searches with it and requires this entry in the top three.

allOf.description: A `planned` entry exists so an agent is told the capability is known and absent rather than inferring it from silence. It cannot carry worked examples of something that does not run, so the full description is required only once it does.
